Ivy: heads-up: weird edge ESM repro where Authorization header is undefined after bundling with esbuild. CJS builds fine. This one is stranger: it only happens when importing the SDK via a default import vs named import.
Marco: default vs named? can you paste the import lines?
Ivy: sure. Works: `import { redwood } from 'sdk'` -> headers ok. Broken: `import sdk from 'sdk'` -> after bundle Authorization missing and sdk retries. dev (ts-node) ok in both forms. only bundles show the difference.
Zoe: interesting. that smells like an interop helper emitting differently for default import helper in ESM builds. TS sometimes emits a small `__importDefault` helper or uses `createRequire` differences depending on `esModuleInterop` and `importsNotUsedAsValues`. If the runtime wrapper was type-only in the SDK d.ts, tree-shaking could collapse it.
Marco: do you have the emitted snippet around the request wrapper?
Ivy: yep. Broken ESM bundle: ```
export default function init(a){return{request:function(u,o){o=o||{};const h=o.headers||{};/* o.auth undefined here */}}}
```
Working CJS bundle: ```
exports.init=function(a){return{request:function(u,o){o=o||{};const h=o.headers||{};h.Authorization=o.auth?.token}}}
```
Ivy: So default import path yields a different helper shape after bundling, and the `auth` prop seems erased if it was only present in an overload/type alias.
Zoe: Check tsconfig: `preserveValueImports`? `importsNotUsedAsValues`? `moduleResolution`? I've seen `preserveValueImports:false` + `esModuleInterop:true` + `minify:true` combos cause the default interop helper to be inlined and then treeshaken if the SDK's runtime-forwarding looks like a no-op to the bundler.
Marco: also check if the SDK export uses a type-only re-export like `export type Client = ...` and a separate `export default client` which makes value traceability weaker. bundlers can disagree on how they see the value being used.
Ivy: tsconfig: module=ESNext, target=ES2022, esModuleInterop=true, preserveValueImports:false, importsNotUsedAsValues=remove. esbuild flags: minify=true, bundle=true, platform=neutral. Switching to `preserveValueImports:true` and minify=false makes the issue disappear.
Zoe: For typing hygiene: avoid overloads that only exist in the typings and not in the runtime signature of the exported factory. If you need overloads for DX, keep a single runtime-visible `options: any` and cast internally. That way bundlers see the runtime prop and won't strip it.
Marco: also test both import forms in samples and docs. If default import behaves differently after bundling we should recommend named imports for edge ESM sample apps until SDK exports are hardened.
Ivy: I'll add a short onboarding note to the edge sample README: "Prefer named imports when bundling for ESM edge runtimes; tsconfig suggestions: preserveValueImports=true, importsNotUsedAsValues=preserve, moduleResolution=bundler; avoid type-only overloads on exported factories."
Zoe: Long-term: SDK should export a tiny non-type-only runtime shim on the default path too, so both `import sdk from 'sdk'` and named import have identical emitted helpers. We should avoid d.ts-only wrappers.
Marco: Agreed. Open an SDK issue to make the default export runtime-visible and add compile+bundle tests (tsc + esbuild) asserting `opts.auth` appears in emitted JS for both import styles.
Ivy: opening repro repo and PR with minimal esbuild configs and a CI job that bundles both import styles. Will drop the repro into devex samples for onboarding.
QA-Bot: CI: edge-esm-default-import-repro #5 failed on node 20 (bundle shows missing Authorization in default import path) :warning:
